rules.name: SQL Injection
rules.description: Dynamic SQL query construction may allow SQL injection.
rules.recommendation: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements.

rules.name: Cross Site Scripting
rules.description: User-controlled data may be rendered as HTML.
rules.recommendation: Escape output and sanitize user input.

rules.name: CSRF Vulnerability
rules.description: State-changing requests may lack CSRF protection.
rules.recommendation: Enable CSRF tokens using Flask-WTF or equivalent.

rules.name: Hardcoded Secret
rules.description: Sensitive credentials are stored in source code.
rules.recommendation: Use environment variables or secret managers.

rules.name: Command Injection
rules.recommendation: Avoid shell execution and validate input.

rules.name: Unsafe YAML Deserialization
rules.description: Unsafe YAML loading can execute malicious objects.

rules.name: Unsafe Pickle Deserialization
rules.description: Pickle can execute arbitrary code during deserialization.

rules.name: Insecure Random
rules.description: Python random module is not cryptographically secure.
rules.recommendation: Use secrets module for security tokens.

rules.name: Path Traversal
rules.description: User-controlled file paths may access unauthorized files.

rules.name: Server Side Request Forgery
rules.description: Server may make requests to attacker-controlled URLs.

rules.name: Template Injection
rules.description: Dynamic templates may execute unsafe expressions.

rules.name: Insecure Authentication
rules.description: HTTP Basic Authentication transmits credentials in an easily decodable form and should only be used over HTTPS with additional protections.
rules.recommendation: Use token-based authentication (OAuth2, JWT, or session tokens) over HTTPS instead of HTTP Basic Auth.

rules.name: Broken Access Control
rules.description: Setting overly permissive file or directory permissions can allow unauthorized users to read, modify, or execute protected resources.
rules.recommendation: Apply the principle of least privilege - grant only the minimum file permissions required for the application to function.
